branch_provenance.syndrome: Chronic Progressive Vascular Lesion of Uncertain Aetiology with Cutaneous Manifestations

state.case_summary:
A man in his 50s presented with a 5-year history of an asymptomatic, gradually enlarging, reddish hematomalike plaque with a brownish peripheral border in his left axilla. The patient reported spontaneous onset of the lesion with no previous history of trauma or any other systemic symptoms. Previous treatment with topical antifungal cream showed no improvement.

Physical examination revealed a nonindurated and well-defined 10 × 8-cm reddish-brown annular plaque with peripheral ecchymosis. No local lymphadenopathy was observed.

- Immunohistochemical studies (from two biopsy specimens):  - Vascular channel endothelial cells were positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40  - Negative for human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) and Wilms tumor 1 (WT1)  - Ki-67 index showed low proliferation in endothelial cells  - Serologic tests:  - HIV: Negative  - Hepatitis B: Negative  - Hepatitis C: Negative- Histologic findings:  - Poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation  - Small dilated, cleftlike, irregular, thin-walled vascular channels dissecting collagen bundles  - No cellular pleomorphism, mitotic figures, or intravascular red blood cells  - Vascular spaces lined with single layer of bland endothelial cells  - Promontory signs present  - Perls Prussian blue staining showed prominent hemosiderin deposits- Images:  Image Title: Clinical image of the left axilla  Image Description: Asymptomatic, reddish hematomalike plaque with a brownish peripheral border

excluded_candidates: Infectious aetiology: negative serologic tests for HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C
Malignant transformation: low proliferation in endothelial cells and no cellular pleomorphism
